verdict.rationale: Fellow documents an official MCP server that lets Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or any connector-capable AI tool query meeting recaps, notes and action items without writing code. Workspace admins govern it: they enable the server, choose which tools are allowed, see last-used timestamps and can revoke connections. The evidence does not name OAuth as the auth mechanism, and it never explicitly says transcripts are exposed through MCP, so the story is not completely covered. Missing for 10: explicit OAuth documentation for MCP connections, explicit transcript access and a documented search tool via MCP, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an official MCP server lets Claude or any MCP client query my meetings — search, transcripts, action items — with OAuth, no glue code

citations.quote: Fellow's Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server allows you to ask your AI Assistant about your meetings, without needing to write any code.
Your favorite AI chatbot like Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor can now tap directly into your meeting recaps, notes, and action items
Fellow's MCP Connector works with any AI tool that supports connectors, so you're never locked into one platform
Workspace owners decide when the MCP Server is enabled, can revoke connections at any time, and see the last-used timestamp for every connection
As a workspace admin, you decide which MCP tools your members’ AI assistants can use.
